extracted.intended_audience: YouTube creators, marketers, and small businesses looking to grow channels
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance on how the YouTube algorithms (homepage, suggested, Shorts, search) work and actionable tips creators can use to improve discovery, engagement, and retention of their videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different algorithms for different discovery surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube does not use a single algorithm for all discovery; there are different algorithms for the homepage, suggested videos, Shorts, and search results, each using a different mix of signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat each surface separately when optimizing: homepage recommendations rely on performance and similar-viewer behavior; suggested videos consider the currently-watched video plus watch history; Shorts uses swipe/short-format signals; search emphasizes relevance to query plus engagement for that search term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction as the core ranking objective
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube aims to surface content that maximizes viewer 'satisfaction' — understanding not just behavior but how viewers feel about their watch time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satisfaction is measured via engagement signals and direct feedback (surveys). Design content to give viewers clear value and a good experience rather than chasing raw engagement metrics alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement signals (behavioral)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube tracks what viewers watch, how long they watch, what they skip over, likes, shares, saving to playlists/queues, and other passive behavioral signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All of these behaviors inform what type of videos a viewer likes and influence future recommendations. Improve watch time, reduce early drop-off, and encourage saves/shares to strengthen these signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct feedback signals (surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube occasionally asks viewers to give direct feedback via quick surveys that influence satisfaction measurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High direct-feedback scores can improve a video's performance and the platform’s willingness to recommend similar content. Creating clearly valuable experiences increases positive survey responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: User preference signals (explicit controls)
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewers can actively influence recommendations via the three-dot menu options like 'Not interested' and 'Don’t recommend channel'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These explicit choices are strong negative signals. Avoid content or thumbnails that trigger 'Not interested' responses; use audience research to align with viewer tastes and reduce negative preference clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homepage recommendation factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Homepage recommendations combine 'Performance' (how well a video engaged/satisfied other viewers with similar interests) and a viewer's watch and search history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appear on a user's homepage, focus on making videos that perform well for viewers similar to your target audience and foster repeated exposure (regular uploads, consistent topic/niche).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested videos ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested videos are chosen based on both the video someone’s currently watching and that viewer’s watch history; the suggested feed may offer filters like 'From [channel]', 'From the series', 'Related topics', 'For you', 'Recently uploaded', and 'Watched'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make your video contextually relevant to other popular videos in your niche (e.g., similar topics/keywords, series structure) and design hooks that make viewers want to continue to the next video in your channel or series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts algorithm metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorts ranking focuses on short-format behaviors: average video watch time, overall engagement, and the percentage of viewers who watch instead of swiping away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Shorts prioritize immediate hooks, high retention through the clip, and engagement actions; optimize the first seconds to prevent swipes and encourage rewatch/share behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube search ranking factors (YouTube SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search rankings depend on how well a video's title, description, and content match the search query and which videos drive the most engagement for that particular search term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keyword-rich, accurate titles and descriptions, include related keywords (without stuffing), name your video file intentionally, and craft content that earns engagement for the target search queries. The first few lines of the description are especially important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience understanding and research
rubrics_metrics.description: Know who your viewers are by using YouTube Analytics (Audience tab), comments, social listening, and audience research tools like SparkToro or competitor analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look beyond raw metrics (watch time) to comments and qualitative signals to discover what viewers emotionally connect with. If you lack YouTube data, use insights from other platforms to infer audience preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick a niche and set expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Give viewers a clear, consistent reason to return by picking a niche and setting expectations about what your channel delivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use frameworks like the 'XY premise' ('This is a [Project type] about [Topic]. Unlike other [Project types] about [Topic], only we [Unique Proposition]') to define your uniqueness. Consistency across videos helps retention across the catalog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep videos focused (narrow topicality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid packing multiple unrelated ideas into a single video; stick to one or two topics so the algorithm can match your content to viewers with specific interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow focus improves the algorithm's ability to place your video in the right viewer cohorts; being too broad can reduce the precision of recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design the viewer journey (promote next videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: Growth is driven by getting viewers to click one video and then stay for the next — plan content to guide viewers to what they should watch next.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cards, verbal prompts, links in descriptions, playlists, series structure, and mentions of older uploads to create clear paths that encourage multiple views and increase catalog depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles: clear, keyword-rich, accurate
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles must both catch attention and help YouTube understand the video's topic; use searchable keywords, be accurate, and keep readability on mobile in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keyword research (YouTube suggestions, Google Trends), avoid misleading titles (clickbait) that cause quick bounces, and aim for concise phrasing that displays well on small screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptions: informative front-loaded metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: The first few lines of the description are what viewers and the algorithm see first; pick one or two main words, include related keywords, and give each video a unique description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid irrelevant keywords or stuffing. Use timestamps, links, and context in the opening lines. A unique, accurate description helps YouTube differentiate your video from similar content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thumbnails: custom, expressive, consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom thumbnails are critical (YouTube says 90% of top-performing videos use custom thumbnails). Thumbnails should be expressive, not overwhelming, use a few readable words, and adhere to community guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test thumbnails on both mobile and desktop, use readable fonts, keep a consistent style for recognizability, and avoid imagery or text that could trigger guideline strikes or viewer 'Not interested' clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a better viewing experience (accessibility & navigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve retention and satisfaction with subtitles/closed captions, chapters/timestamps, and smooth navigation so viewers can find the parts they want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add captions (auto-edit or SRT upload) for accessibility and noisy environments; include timestamps in the description (mm:ss) and organize longer videos with chapters to reduce drop-off and increase perceived value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach viewers in different languages (dubbing & subtitles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple audio tracks (dubbing) or translated subtitles to broaden reach; creators who dub at least 80% of their catalog in a language often see stronger results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with translated subtitles to test new audiences, then consider focused dubbing for languages where you can reach catalog depth (aim for ~80% of catalog in a language rather than small slices across many languages). Use translation tools or services to scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid gaming the algorithm; optimize for audience
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s 'no gaming the YouTube algorithm' — rather, work with it by creating for your audience and overlapping your creative voice with what viewers want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize audience understanding and high-quality viewing experiences over tricks. Misleading metadata or clickbait may yield short-term clicks but will harm long-term performance via poor retention or negative preference signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage platform experiments for new creators
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube runs experiments to promote new/small creators; the platform may surface new content to relevant viewers to help channels find an audience faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small channels should focus on creating content that performs well for a specific audience and let the platform's experiments and catalog depth drive more impressions and data — you don't always need a large following to be recommended.
